subject: maths
title: Adding and Subtracting 2- and 3-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Year 3 Adding and Subtracting Worksheets: Partitioning, Regrouping and the Jump Strategy
standard_text: Add and subtract two- and three-digit numbers using place value to partition, rearrange and regroup numbers to assist in calculations without a calculator
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on adding and subtracting two- and three-digit numbers, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M3N03): the split strategy, MAB, regrouping, subtracting across a zero, the jump strategy and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key. Great NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Partition into hundreds, tens and ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: 10 ones make 1 ten and 10 tens make 1 hundred. Adding: if a column makes 10 or more, regroup 1 into the next column. Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column.
body_html:
The idea: partition, then put it back together

Every number is made of hundreds, tens and ones. Partition (split) the numbers. Add the hundreds, the tens and the ones. Then put the parts back together.

If the ones make 10 or more, regroup: 10 ones make 1 ten.

The column method: regroup when a column makes 10 or more

Put ones under ones, tens under tens and hundreds under hundreds. Start with the ones on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 into the next column.

Subtracting: regroup when the top digit is smaller

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column as 10.

Across a zero: if there are 0 tens, regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens first. Then regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. The 0 becomes 9.

The jump strategy on an empty number line

Start at the first number. Jump the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Rearrange

What is 38 + 145 + 62?

You can add in any order. 38 + 62 = 100. Then 100 + 145 = 245.

Answer: 245

Near a hundred

What is 456 + 199?

199 is 1 less than 200. 456 + 200 = 656. Take away the extra 1: 655.

Answer: 655

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the regrouped ten (367 + 258 = 515)Write the regrouped 1 under the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one (452 − 178 = 326)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Not regrouping across a zero (402 − 158 = 254)Regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens first. The 0 becomes 9
Adding tens as if they were ones (245 + 132 = 350)The 3 in 132 is 3 tens, worth 30: 245 + 132 = 377

faq.q: What does Year 3 learn about adding and subtracting in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Students add and subtract two- and three-digit numbers without a calculator. They partition, rearrange and regroup numbers, for example using the split strategy, the jump strategy and the column method.
Regrouping means swapping 10 of one place for 1 of the next, such as 10 ones for 1 ten. It is also called trading, and older books call it carrying or borrowing.

faq.q: How do you subtract across a zero, like 402 − 158?
faq.a: Regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens, then 1 ten as 10 ones. 402 becomes 3 hundreds, 9 tens and 12 ones, and the answer is 244.

faq.q: Is adding and subtracting on the Year 3 NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: Yes. Adding and subtracting with two- and three-digit numbers is part of the Year 3 Australian Curriculum, which the numeracy test is based on, and many questions are word problems.

sets.title: Rearrange and use the jump strategy

items.q: Which two numbers should you add first to make 100?  47 + 286 + 53
Which has the same answer as 156 + 237?
items.e: You can add numbers in any order. 237 + 156 = 393, the same as 156 + 237. 165 and 273 have digits swapped, so they are different numbers.

items.q: Rearrange to make a friendly number first. What is 38 + 145 + 62?
items.e: Rearrange: add 38 + 62 first to make 100. Then 100 + 145 = 245.

items.q: Rearrange to make a friendly number first. What is 27 + 356 + 73?

items.q: Count on to find the difference. What is 425 − 398?
items.e: The numbers are close, so count on from 398. 398 + 2 = 400, then 400 + 25 = 425. 2 + 25 = 27. So 425 − 398 = 27.

items.q: Count on to find the difference. What is 703 − 685?
items.e: The numbers are close, so count on from 685. 685 + 15 = 700, then 700 + 3 = 703. 15 + 3 = 18. So 703 − 685 = 18.

items.q: 199 is 1 less than 200. What is 456 + 199?
items.e: Add 200, then take away the extra 1. 456 + 200 = 656. 656 − 1 = 655.

items.q: 298 is 2 less than 300. What is 347 + 298?

items.q: 198 is 2 less than 200. What is 532 − 198?
items.e: Take away 200. You took away 2 too many, so add 2 back. 532 − 200 = 332. 332 + 2 = 334.

items.e: Altogether means add. 236 + 158 = 394. Check: 394 − 158 = 236.

items.q: Noah’s book has 400 pages. He read 132 pages on the weekend and 89 pages on Monday. How many pages are left to read?
items.e: Step 1, pages read: 132 + 89 = 221. Step 2, pages left: 400 − 221 = 179.

items.q: A cricket club’s junior teams scored 245 runs on Saturday. On Sunday they scored 136 more runs than on Saturday. How many runs did they score over the weekend?
items.e: Step 1, Sunday’s runs: 245 + 136 = 381. Step 2, both together: 245 + 381 = 626.
